title: Visnupurana, book 4

reply:
Only verse 73 states a relation. Its subject is unnamed in the verse itself: the king is not named, and the verse gives only "kumāraṃ cāyuṣam", so the son is Āyus, given by Urvaśī to "asmai" (him, a king). The verse does not say who the father is. The son Āyus and the mother Urvaśī are named, but the text says Urvaśī gave Āyus to him. That does not say outright that Āyus is Urvaśī's son, because "dadau" is only giving.

Verse 74 says she conceived "pañca putrotpattaye" with "tena rājñā", but no names are given. Verse 93 says the king was not separated from Urvaśī, which is narration and not a kinship statement. Neither verse names the king, so no relation can be stated for him.

The only possible statement is that Āyus is Urvaśī's son. That is an inference from "gave", and the verse does not say it. I leave it out.
